chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Safwan ibn Yahya and Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is no harm in a woman wearing the two khalkhals (ankle bracelets) and the mask (face veil), and this does not contradict the first report, because the dislike in the first report was only directed towards what was not the custom of women among the jewelry. As for what has become their custom, there is no harm in it.

key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَة: Dislike or mild prohibition in fiqh

ai.seo_question: What jewelry is permissible for a woman to wear during Hajj Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration in *al-Istibsar* to resolve apparent contradictions in hadith regarding women's adornment during Hajj, establishing the principle of 'urf' (custom) as a key determinant in fiqh. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between customary items like ankle bracelets and face veils, which are permissible, and non-customary jewelry, which remains disliked, thereby harmonizing the reports. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextualizing legal rulings based on prevailing social norms of the time.
